newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis says budget should allow lower rates.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis says budget should allow lower rates.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Wednesday that he believed the government's 1997 budget would pave the way for further falls in interest rates.
Asked by Reuters Financial Television whether the budget, which aims to cut the public deficit to below three percent of GDP, would allow for lower interest rates, Arthuis replied: "Yes, certainly."
Arthuis said the government's austerity policies had already led to big falls in interest rates.
"We have obtained a substantial reduction of interest rates," he said. "Less than one year ago, short-term rates were 7.5 percent. Today, they are approximately 3.6-3.7 percent."
He said the fall in rates was a boon to companies and local authorities seeking to borrow money.
Arthuis said the deficit-cutting budget showed financial markets the government would meet the Maastricht criteria for monetary union.
"We are in a position to respect the three percent deficit (of GDP target). "We will be ready for the single currency on January 1, 1999."
Arthuis rejected suggestions that the government was using creative accounting methods to reduce its deficit by transferring funds from state-owned France Telecom.
"It is a very transparent operation and we are applying the basic rules of European accountancy," Arthuis said.

France Telecom is making a one-time contribution of 37.5 billion francs to state revenues in exchange for the government taking over the company's pension liabilities ahead of its partial privatisation. The money will be counted as revenue when calculating France's total public deficit.
